function.name: create_file
function.description: Create a new file with the supplied complete content. The creation is staged for review and is not written until approved.

path.description: New file path relative to the workspace root.

content.description: Complete content for the new file.

function.name: delete_file
function.description: Delete one file. The deletion is staged for explicit review and the file remains unchanged until approved.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root.

function.name: replace_in_file
function.description: Replace one exact text string in a file. The match must include exact whitespace and indentation. The change is staged for review and is not written until approved.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root.

old_text.description: Exact text to replace; it must occur exactly once.

function.name: run_command
function.description: Stage a shell command to run in the workspace (or a subdirectory of it) — for package installs, project scaffolding, and build/test commands. The command does not run until the user reviews and approves it.

command.description: The exact shell command to run.

cwd.description: Directory to run it in, relative to the workspace root. Defaults to the workspace root.

function.name: find_files
function.description: Search filenames and relative paths inside the workspace to locate a file without knowing its exact path.

query.description: Filename, partial name, or natural-language term to search for.

function.name: list_directory
function.description: List the contents of a directory in the workspace (directories first, then files, alphabetically).

path.description: Directory to list, relative to the workspace root. Defaults to the workspace root.

how are tool calls staged for approval in this codebase?

Mutating tool calls (create_file, replace_in_file, delete_file, run_command) don't execute immediately — they're recorded as a pending patch or command run in the DB and emitted over SSE as patch_staged/command_staged, and only actually applied once the user calls the approve endpoint.
